## Learning Objectives {.unnumbered}

{{< include ../learning_objectives/0640-containers-uv.qmd >}}

## Download the images before you start {.unnumbered}

The examples in this chapter build on two images.
Start Docker first (on macOS and Windows, open Docker Desktop),
then download (pull) them before you start:

```bash
docker pull ubuntu:24.04
docker pull ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.7
```

## The project

This chapter puts the Python packages of a small uv project into a Docker image.
It is a uv project like the ones in [Virtual environments: Python (uv)](0520-virtual-environments-python-uv.qmd),
and its files are in the book repository's `demos/docker-uv/end` folder.
`hello.py` prints a message with the [cowsay](https://pypi.org/project/cowsay/) package:

```{.python}
import cowsay

cowsay.cow("Hello from Python in my image!")
```

`pyproject.toml` lists the package with an exact version,
and `add-bounds = "exact"` makes `uv add` write exact versions too
(see [Exact versions with uv](0545-virtual-environments-python-uv-exact-pins.qmd)):

```{.toml}
[project]
name = "docker-uv"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    "cowsay==6.1",
]

[tool.uv]
# `uv add` writes an exact version (==)
add-bounds = "exact"
```

`.python-version` holds `3.14`,
and `uv.lock` locks cowsay and everything it needs.
On your computer, `uv run` creates the project's `.venv` folder and runs the script:

```bash
uv run hello.py
```

```out
Using CPython 3.14.3
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Installed 1 package in 9ms
  ______________________________
| Hello from Python in my image! |
  ==============================
                              \
                               \
                                 ^__^
                                 (oo)\_______
                                 (__)\       )\/\
                                     ||----w |
                                     ||     ||
```

## A `Dockerfile` for a uv project

Here is the project's `Dockerfile`.
Its uv lines are the same as in [docker-uv-renv](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv),
the example project that [Docker Compose](0650-containers-docker-compose.qmd) uses:

```{.dockerfile}
# Ubuntu Linux, with no Python: uv installs Python itself
FROM ubuntu:24.04

# install python uv
# https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker/#installing-uv
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.7 /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/

# The project is mounted over /workspace, so the packages go in /opt
WORKDIR /workspace

# python packages in /opt/venv
ENV UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version ./
# --locked: stop if uv.lock doesn't match pyproject.toml
RUN uv sync --locked
```

- `FROM ubuntu:24.04` starts from Ubuntu Linux, which has no Python.
  uv installs the Python version that `.python-version` asks for.
- `COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.7` copies the `uv` and `uvx` programs
  out of the image that uv publishes,
  as [uv's Docker guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/docker/#installing-uv) shows.
  The tag pins uv's version, the same way a lockfile pins a package's.
- `WORKDIR /workspace` makes `/workspace` the working directory,
  for the rest of the build and for containers that run from the image.
  You will mount your project folder there.
- `ENV UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv` tells uv to put the project's virtual environment
  in `/opt/venv`, instead of in `.venv` inside the project folder
  (see [uv's environment variables](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/environment/#uv_project_environment)).
  The section after next shows why.
- `COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock .python-version ./` copies only the files that list the packages,
  not the code.
  Editing `hello.py` then never reinstalls the packages,
  because the `COPY` and `RUN` steps above it have not changed
  (see [Building images](0630-containers-building.qmd)).
- `RUN uv sync --locked` installs Python and the packages listed in `uv.lock`.
  `--locked` stops the build if `uv.lock` does not match `pyproject.toml`.

```bash
docker build --tag docker-uv .
```

The first `FROM` line is uv's image, which `COPY --from` reads `uv` from.
To see what `uv sync` printed,
build with `--progress=plain`, which shows each step's own output,
and `--no-cache`, which runs every step again instead of reusing its layer.
Here is the `uv sync` step:

```bash
docker build --progress=plain --no-cache --tag docker-uv .
```

```out
#11 [stage-0 5/5] RUN uv sync --locked
#11 0.309 Downloading cpython-3.14.10-linux-aarch64-gnu (download) (29.2MiB)
#11 3.201  Downloaded cpython-3.14.10-linux-aarch64-gnu (download)
#11 3.352 Using CPython 3.14.10
#11 3.352 Creating virtual environment at: /opt/venv
#11 3.359 Resolved 2 packages in 2ms
#11 3.434 Prepared 1 package in 74ms
#11 3.451 Installed 1 package in 16ms
```

uv downloaded Python 3.14,
created the virtual environment at `/opt/venv`,
and installed cowsay into it.

## Run the project in a container

The image has the packages but not the code.
Mount the project folder at `/workspace`,
and run the script with `uv run` in place of the image's default command
(see [Running containers](0620-containers-running.qmd)):

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv uv run hello.py
```

## Windows (Git Bash)

```bash
docker run --rm -v "/$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv uv run hello.py
```

## Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/workspace" docker-uv uv run hello.py
```
:::

```out
  ______________________________
| Hello from Python in my image! |
  ==============================
                              \
                               \
                                 ^__^
                                 (oo)\_______
                                 (__)\       )\/\
                                     ||----w |
                                     ||     ||
```

:::{.callout-note title="Why `/$(pwd)` in Git Bash?"}
Git Bash turns command-line arguments that start with `/` into Windows paths,
so `/workspace` could reach Docker as `C:/Program Files/Git/workspace`.
Doubling the first slash, which `/$(pwd)` does, stops that
(see "Known issues" in the [Git for Windows release notes](https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/blob/main/ReleaseNotes.md#known-issues)).
:::

## Why the packages go in `/opt/venv`

Without a mount, `/workspace` holds the three files the `Dockerfile` copied:

```bash
docker run --rm docker-uv ls -a
```

```out
.
..
.python-version
pyproject.toml
uv.lock
```

With the project folder mounted, `/workspace` shows your computer's folder instead,
including the `.venv` folder that `uv run` created on your computer:

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv ls -a
```

## Windows (Git Bash)

```bash
docker run --rm -v "/$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv ls -a
```

## Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/workspace" docker-uv ls -a
```
:::

```out
.
..
.gitignore
.python-version
.venv
Dockerfile
hello.py
pyproject.toml
uv.lock
```

A mount hides whatever the image had at that path.
If the image kept its packages in `/workspace/.venv`,
the mount would hide them.
Worse, uv in the container would find your computer's `.venv` instead,
which holds a program for your computer's operating system, not for Linux.
On a Mac:

```bash
file .venv/bin/python3
```

```out
.venv/bin/python3: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64
```

With the `ENV` line left out of the `Dockerfile`,
running `uv run hello.py` with the mount printed these lines, among others:

```out
Removed virtual environment at: .venv
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
```

uv deleted your computer's `.venv` and made a Linux one in its place,
which no longer works on your computer.
With `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv`, the container leaves `.venv` alone
and uses the environment that the image built:

::: {.panel-tabset group="shell"}
## macOS and Linux

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"
```

## Windows (Git Bash)

```bash
docker run --rm -v "/$(pwd):/workspace" docker-uv uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"
```

## Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/workspace" docker-uv uv run python -c "import sys; print(sys.prefix)"
```
:::

```out
/opt/venv
```
